newsitem.title: USA: CME traders say USDA data neutral-bullish for hogs.
newsitem.headline: CME traders say USDA data neutral-bullish for hogs.

text.p: Chicago Mercantile Exchange livestock futures traders said Thursday's U.S. Department of Agriculture Hogs and Pigs Report should be neutral to nearby CME hog and pork belly futures and slightly bullish to deferred contracts.
"We are too cheap in the back months (of the futures)," said Phil Stanley, an independent livestock analyst.

Traders and analysts assembled at the CME were reluctant to offer a point call for Monday's futures, saying any changes in Taiwan's hog situation over the three-day weekend would have a greater influence on futures than the report's data.

USDA data in the report's three main categories were close to analysts' expectations, but the report's farrowing projections and December-February pig crop estimate were less than the averages of analysts' estimates.

USDA reported all hogs on U.S. farms as of March 1 at 99 percent of a year ago versus the analysts' average estimate of 99.2. USDA's kept for breeding figure was 101 percent versus analysts' average of 101.4 and USDA's kept for marketing figure was 99 percent of a year ago, the same as the analysts' average estimate.

USDA's December-February farrowings were 98 percent of a year ago, less than analysts' average of 100.2. Also, USDA's March-May farrowing intentions estimate was 100 percent, also below analysts' average projection of 102.9 percent and USDA's December-February pig crop was 100 percent, under analysts' average of 101.4.
